newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BIL sees 1996 net up 9% at 3.105 bln Lfr.
newsitem.headline: BIL sees 1996 net up 9% at 3.105 bln Lfr.

text.p: Luxembourg bank Banque Internationale a Luxembourg (BIL) expects 1996 net profit to have risen around nine percent to 3.105 billion Luxembourg francs, chief executive officer Andre Roelants told a news conference on Wednesday.
BIL is majority-owned by Belgium's Dexia CC, formerly known as Credit Communal/Gemeentekrediet, the sister-bank to France's Credit Local de France.
Roelants, who replaced Jean Krier as CEO last month, said once accounts were audited the rise in profit could lie anywhere between eight and 12 percent.
"1996 was a very good year for the bank, especially the second half," he said.

BIL is destined to become the private banking arm of the new Franco-Belgian Dexia Group. Roelants said 1997 would see it expand its fund management activities, setting up two new companies and a Cayman Islands branch.
BIL also plans to develop a system for secure transactions over the bank's intranet and over the internet, he said.
